sources.title: ADR schemes' performance
sources.evidence_kind: quarterly alternative dispute resolution KPI results
sources.evidence_location: official HTML performance table and approval sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom communications and postal sectors
facts: Ofcom publishes quarterly KPI results for CISAS and Communications Ombudsman
Communications Ombudsman answered 95% of Q2 2026 calls within two minutes
Communications Ombudsman answered 98% of Q2 2026 calls within five minutes
Less than 1% of accepted case decisions were issued later than eight weeks
limitations: ADR performance is not broadband coverage or provider orderability evidence
Scheme processes differ and KPI comparisons require the published caveat

sources.title: Service quality
facts: Index lists the Q1 2026 broadband complaints release dated 23 July 2026
Index lists ADR performance updated 23 July 2026
Index lists automatic compensation guidance updated 20 July 2026
Index lists Communications Market 2026 published 30 June 2026
limitations: Index identity and dates do not substitute for publication contents
Service-quality publications do not establish address-level coverage

sources.title: Latest telecoms and pay-TV complaints revealed - Q4 2025
facts: Release covers October to December 2025
Broadband and landline complaints decreased from the previous quarter
TalkTalk and Vodafone were the most complained-about broadband providers
Plusnet and Virgin Media were the least complained-about broadband providers
limitations: Complaint rates measure consumer dissatisfaction rather than coverage
Provider rankings are quarter-specific and relative to customer bases

sources.title: Statement: Review of ADR in the telecoms sector
sources.evidence_location: official HTML decision and implementation sections
facts: Providers received nine months to implement the revised ADR access timeframe
The new timeframe applies to complaints raised on or after 8 April 2026
Updated ADR scheme KPIs took effect from Q4 2025
Ofcom re-approved Communications Ombudsman and CISAS
limitations: ADR rules are consumer-protection evidence, not service availability

sources.title: Automatic compensation: What you need to know
sources.evidence_location: official HTML signatory and eligibility sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom participating broadband and landline providers
facts: Scheme provides compensation without a customer having to request it
Published signatories include BT, EE, Hyperoptic, Plusnet, Sky, TalkTalk, Utility Warehouse, Virgin Media, Vodafone and Zen
Compensation applies to defined service-failure situations
Compensation amounts increase annually with inflation
limitations: Signatory status does not prove address availability or network quality
Eligibility depends on the incident and provider participation
